title: The Two Friends
text:
La Fontaine sets this fable in the faraway land of Monomotapa, where, he says, two true friends once lived. Whatever one owned belonged to the other.

One night, while everyone was asleep, one of the friends jumped out of bed in alarm, ran through the dark streets to his friend's house and woke the servants. The friend in bed was astonished. He got up, took his purse and his sword, and went to meet his visitor.

"You never run about at this hour," he said. "You are a man who values his sleep. Something must have happened. Have you lost money gambling? Here is my purse. Have you quarreled with someone? Here is my sword, and I will go with you. Or are you lonely tonight? Here is a beautiful slave girl; I can send her to you."

"No," said his friend, "it is none of that. I thank you for all of it. But I fell asleep and dreamed that you looked sad. I was afraid it might be true, and I could not rest. That bad dream is why I came running."

Which of the two loved the other more, La Fontaine asks, and leaves the question to the reader.
lesson: Good friends pay attention and come before they are called. Offer help freely, and do not wait for someone you love to ask.
source: Jean de La Fontaine, Fables, Book VIII, Fable 11
